mechanism: For each fine level l in {2,3} (level 1 is untouched) the baseline residual r_{i,l} = z_i - sum_{j<l} E_{k_j(i)} is mapped into the Poincare ball B_c^d with fixed curvature c = 1 by the frozen-scale origin exponential v_i = exp_0^c(r_{i,l}/q_l) = tanhc(sqrt(c)||r||/q_l)(r/q_l), and every codebook row by the same map u_k = exp_0^c(E_k/q_l). The train-split directed successor multiset of item i, read from a per-epoch detached ball-point snapshot V_l, gives a tangent behaviour vector t_i = sum_s (w_is/W_i) log_{v_i}^c(V_l[s]) at v_i; its unit direction n_i and its length M_i fix an arc length m_i = min(M_i, 0.5*min_k d_c(v_i,u_k)), identically 0 when BEHAV=off. Every code is then displaced inside the ball along the item's direction, q_{i,k} = u_k (+) exp_0^c((m_i/2) n_i), a Mobius translation by a ball element whose origin distance is exactly m_i, and the cost C[i,k] = d_c(v_i, q_{i,k}) is the exact Poincare distance from the item point to the displaced code. C is fed unchanged into the baseline entropy-regularised Sinkhorn with the baseline epsilon, uniform item marginal and balanced code marginal; the plan P is kept (no argmin of C replaces it), the baseline plan extraction turns P into indices, the decoder is fed the chosen raw codeword through the baseline straight-through estimator, and the baseline RQ-VAE loss trains encoder and codebook. Behaviour enters only as a detached, once-per-epoch field; c = 0 is the contract's Euclidean limit branch. The geometry is the contract's operator family verbatim: d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(clip(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||, 0, 1-1e-5)), exp_0^c, log_x^c, and Mobius addition, with the artanh clip and tanhc/atanhc limits of the numerical contract.

computations.name: level_residual
computations.definition: r_{i,l} = z_i - sum_{j=1}^{l-1} E_{k_j(i)}, l in {2,3}; z_i is the encoder latent of item i and k_j(i) the baseline assignment at level j
inputs: E_{k_j(i)} for j < l (B x d)
computations.note: Baseline residual reused unchanged; k_j(i) are integer constants, so the gradient reaches z_i and the coarse rows E_{k_j}. Level 1 is not touched by the mechanism.

computations.name: scale_q_l
computations.definition: q_l = percentile_95({ ||r_{i,l}||_2 : i in the training split }), evaluated once at epoch 0 and frozen as a buffer
computations.note: One frozen scalar per level; no gradient, no update, no test-split data.

computations.name: ball_lift
computations.definition: v_i = exp_0^c(r_{i,l}/q_l) = tanhc(sqrt(c)||r_{i,l}||/q_l) * (r_{i,l}/q_l), with tanhc(a) = tanh(a)/a and tanhc(0) = 1
computations.note: Identical to the spec's (1/sqrt(c))*tanh(sqrt(c)||r||/q_l)*r/||r||; the tanhc form is the contract's explicit zero-norm limit, no 1e-12 guard.

computations.name: code_lift
computations.note: Same map as the item lift, applied to the codebook; this is the only route by which codebook rows see the displaced cost.

computations.name: successor_snapshot
computations.definition: V_l[s] = no_grad( exp_0^c(r_{s,l}/q_l) ) for every training item s, computed once per epoch from the epoch-start encoder and epoch-start assignments
inputs: training-split z_s and r_{s,l} at epoch start
computations.note: Detached per-epoch constant; the behaviour field refreshes once per epoch and never carries gradient (see missing item on which level-l residual defines V_l at level 3).

computations.name: behaviour_tangent
computations.definition: t_i = (1/W_i) * sum_s w_is * log_{v_i}^c(V_l[s]), where W_i = sum_s w_is and log_x^c(y) = (2/(sqrt(c)*lambda_x^c)) * atanhc(sqrt(c)||w||) * w with w = (-x)(+)_c y and lambda_x^c = 2/(1-c||x||^2)
computations.output: t_i (B x d) tangent vector at v_i
computations.note: The behaviour entry point. Detached immediately, so it is a per-epoch constant; W_i > 0 assumed (empty successor rows are a missing definition).

computations.name: behaviour_direction
computations.definition: n_i = t_i / max(||t_i||, 1e-12), so n_i = 0 iff t_i = 0
computations.output: n_i (B x d), unit or zero
computations.note: Detached. The 1e-12 is inside max, i.e. a direction guard, not a stand-in for a zero-norm limit of the geometry.

computations.name: behaviour_magnitude
computations.note: Which norm (Euclidean coordinate norm of the tangent vector, or the Riemannian lambda_{v_i}||t_i|| of contract section 3) is not stated - see missing.

computations.name: nearest_code_distance
computations.definition: d_nn_i = min_{k in [K]} d_c(v_i, u_k) with d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(clip(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)_c y||, 0, 1-1e-5))
computations.note: Subgradient only through the argmin row; equals the BEHAV=off cost row minimum.

computations.name: arc_length
computations.definition: m_i = min(M_i, 0.5 * d_nn_i); BEHAV=off sets m_i = 0
computations.note: First branch is constant (detached M_i); whether the 0.5*d_nn_i branch is detached is not stated - see missing.

computations.name: displacement
computations.definition: Delta_i = exp_0^c((m_i/2) n_i) = (1/sqrt(c))*tanh(sqrt(c)*m_i/2)*n_i, which satisfies d_c(0, Delta_i) = 2*||(m_i/2)n_i|| = m_i by contract identity 4
computations.note: Constant per item: m_i and n_i are detached. The half factor is the contract's tangent normalisation, so the translation's origin distance equals m_i exactly.

computations.name: displaced_code
computations.output: q (B x 256 x d) inside B_c^d
computations.note: Differentiable in u_k; Delta_i is a constant, so no gradient to the behaviour field. BEHAV=off gives Delta_i = 0 and q_{i,k} = u_k.

computations.name: poincare_cost
computations.definition: C[i,k] = d_c(v_i, q_{i,k}) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( min(sqrt(c)||(-v_i)(+)_c q_{i,k}||, 1-1e-5) )
computations.note: The metric. Contract form with the factor 2; the clip saturates and zeroes the gradient when a point sits on the boundary.

computations.name: sinkhorn_plan
computations.definition: P = argmin_{P in U(a,b)} <P,C> + epsilon * sum_{i,k} P_{ik}(log P_{ik} - 1), with a_i = 1/B uniform item marginal and b the baseline balanced code marginal, solved by the baseline iteration, plan returned
computations.note: Same epsilon, same marginals, same extraction as the baseline; no argmin of C is substituted for the plan.

computations.name: assignment
computations.definition: k_l(i) = baseline_plan_to_index(P)[i] (the baseline row rule applied to the plan)
computations.note: Discrete, no gradient, no straight-through: the assignment is a decision, exactly as in the baseline.

computations.name: reconstruction
computations.definition: y_i^{(l)} = z_i^{(l)} + (E_{k_l(i)} - z_i^{(l)}).detach(); the decoder receives the sum of the per-level straight-through codewords and never the displaced q_{i,k} nor u_k
computations.output: decoder input (B x d), reconstruction x_hat (B x D_out)
computations.note: The chosen raw codeword is what is reconstructed; the displacement only re-weights the assignment.

computations.name: loss_total
computations.definition: L = L_RQVAE(assigned codes) per the baseline definition, i.e. reconstruction + commitment ||r_{i,l} - sg(E_{k_l(i)})||^2 + codebook ||sg(r_{i,l}) - E_{k_l(i)}||^2 over l in {2,3}, plus whatever plan term the baseline already has
computations.note: No term in C or in q_{i,k} is defined, so the gradient statement 'through v_i and u_k only' has no carrier - see missing.

computations.name: switch_behaviour
computations.definition: BEHAV=off sets t_i = 0 for every item, hence n_i = 0, M_i = 0, m_i = 0, Delta_i = 0, q_{i,k} = u_k and C[i,k] = d_c(v_i, u_k); BEHAV=on uses the tangent field
computations.note: Pure branch, no gradient. The arm is unit-checked and not trained.

computations.name: switch_geometry
computations.definition: GEOM=euclid sets c := 0, selecting the contract's Euclidean limit: (+) becomes +, exp_0^0(v) = v, log_x^0(y) = y - x, d_0(x,y) = 2||x-y||; GEOM=poincare keeps c = 1
computations.output: the operator family used by every computation above
computations.note: Branch selection. The spec's flat form C = ||(v_i-u_k) - m_i n_i||_2 is not the c->0 limit of the stated branch and its lift has no stated limit - see missing.

inputs: r_{i,l}: level-l residuals of the batch (B x d)
E_l: level-l codebook rows (256 x d)
S_i = {(s, w_is)}: frozen training-split directed successor rows with counts
V_l: per-epoch detached successor ball-point snapshot (N_train x d)
baseline Sinkhorn configuration (epsilon, uniform item marginal, balanced code marginal, plan extraction)
baseline RQ-VAE loss terms and optimizer configuration
outputs: C: B x 256 cost matrix of Poincare distances to the behaviour-displaced codes
P: B x 256 balanced Sinkhorn plan
intermediates for the switches: v_l, u_l, t_i, n_i, M_i, d_nn_i, m_i, Delta_i, q (B x 256 x d)
parameters: baseline Sinkhorn epsilon, marginals and plan extraction (values taken from the baseline, not restated)
switches: BEHAV: off sets t_i = 0 for every item, hence n_i = 0, M_i = 0, m_i = 0, Delta_i = 0, q_{i,k} = u_k and C[i,k] = d_c(v_i, u_k); the balanced Sinkhorn plan and the curvature are unchanged. The arm is unit-checked and not trained.

GEOM: euclid sets c := 0 and switches every operator to the contract's Euclidean limit ((+) -> +, exp_0^0(v) = v, log_x^0(y) = y-x, d_0(x,y) = 2||x-y||) with the same behaviour field; poincare keeps c = 1. The arm is unit-checked and not trained, and its stated flat cost does not match this limit (see missing).
excluded: Level 1: no cost, no drift, the baseline is executed verbatim
Any signal from outside the training split: no user ids, no timestamps, no popularity, no test-split successors
Any pruning or top-K on the successor rows: all successors with their counts are kept
Any learned per-item weights or attention over successors: fixed counts only
Any Fréchet mean or barycentre: the successor aggregation is a weighted mean of tangent vectors at a single base point v_i
Any straight-through estimator inside the transport path: the assignment is a genuine discrete decision
Any change to the Sinkhorn epsilon, the uniform item marginal, the balanced code marginal or the plan extraction
Any reimplementation of exp/log/distance/projection outside the geometry contract module
Training of the BEHAV=off and GEOM=euclid ablation arms

continuous_surface.name: poincare_displaced_cost_2d
continuous_surface.note: a0 = -x0 (the point (-x) enters the Mobius difference); p is the detached displacement Delta_i = (1/sqrt(c))*tanh(sqrt(c)*m_i/2)*n_i supplied as a constant.

missing: The norm in M_i = ||t_i||: Euclidean coordinate norm of the stored tangent vector, or the Riemannian norm lambda_{v_i}||t_i|| that contract section 3 requires for tangent norms. m_i, Delta_i and hence the displacement length differ by the factor lambda_{v_i} = 2/(1-c||v_i||^2) between the two readings.

The GEOM=euclid branch: the c->0 limit of the lift is v = r/q_l (a linear map, not the 'bounded Euclidean radial map' the spec claims; ||v|| can exceed 1), the limit of the displacement is (m_i/2) n_i, and the contract fixes d_0(x,y) = 2||x-y|| - whereas the spec states C[i,k] = ||(v_i-u_k) - m_i n_i||_2, which differs by a factor 2 in the displacement and a factor 2 in the metric and leaves the lift's limit unstated. Which convention governs the flat branch is undefined.

Whether the cost C, or the plan P, enters the total loss, and with what coefficient and functional form. With loss = baseline RQ-VAE loss on the assigned codes and the decoder fed the chosen raw codeword, the plan is converted to an index with no gradient, so C carries no gradient at all and the stated 'gradients flow through v_i and u_k only' has no carrier.

The content of the per-epoch snapshot at level 3: which level-2 codes define r_{s,3} for the snapshot (the epoch-start assignment or the current batch's), and whether the snapshot is taken before the epoch's first update or refreshed during the epoch. Also how V_l is defined for training items that receive no level-2 assignment.
Items i with an empty successor row (W_i = 0): no rule is given for t_i, which is a division by W_i in the stated formula.

Whether the 0.5*d_nn_i term inside m_i is detached: only t_i and n_i are declared detached, but d_nn_i is built from the live v_i and u_k, so the clamp could carry gradient into the encoder and codebook.
